chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shireh, from Ali ibn Suleyman, who said:

I wrote to him asking him about the deceased who dies at Arafat, whether he should be buried at Arafat or transferred to the Haram, so which of the two is superior? So he wrote: 'Carry him to the Haram and bury him, for it is superior.'

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior, more virtuous or preferable in religious merit
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Haram, referring to the sacred precincts of Mecca
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Is it better to bury a deceased pilgrim in Arafat or transfer them to Mecca?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith clarifies the preference for interring a pilgrim who dies at Arafat within the sanctified precincts of Mecca (the Haram) rather than leaving them at the site of standing. This ruling underscores the enduring spiritual merit of the Haram's proximity to the Kaaba, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sanctity of the holy sites even in matters of death and burial.
